account: Blackpool Council's Project Amber, launched in 2019 under the Local Council Roads Innovation Group, uses high-definition road imagery to detect potholes and prioritize repairs. The Blackpool Unlimited page calls it artificial-intelligence technology piloted in Anchorsholme and Bispham. It states that since summer 2019, 5,145 potholes were filled in North Shore for just under £450,000 against £1.5 million by traditional methods. The Department for Transport's release of 26 September 2024 says Blackpool was the first authority to use the technology. It had paid up to £1.5 million a year to settle pothole claims and “last year” paid out only £719. The release dates the work only as “last year”. The reduction is credited to the whole program, including surface treatments.

ai_role.statement: Neither source isolates the detection software's contribution. The claims reduction and savings are credited to Project Amber as a whole, which combines imagery surveys with preventive surface treatments. The Blackpool Unlimited page is undated and does not state its operator, so it is treated as a council-adjacent promotional page, not an official report.

fields.account: Blackpool Council's Project Amber, launched in 2019 under the Local Council Roads Innovation Group, uses high-definition road imagery to detect potholes and prioritize repairs. The Blackpool Unlimited page calls it artificial-intelligence technology piloted in Anchorsholme and Bispham. It states that since summer 2019, 5,145 potholes were filled in North Shore for just under £450,000 against £1.5 million by traditional methods. The Department for Transport's release of 26 September 2024 says Blackpool was the first authority to use the technology. It had paid up to £1.5 million a year to settle pothole claims and “last year” paid out only £719. The release dates the work only as “last year”. The reduction is credited to the whole program, including surface treatments.
